researcher_notes: Proposed year = when AES first publicly proposed the LNG import terminal at Outer Brewster Island in Boston Harbor, MA. AES (AES Battery Rock LLC) announced its intention in 2005 to lease/buy Outer Brewster Island and build an LNG import terminal; the proposal was fought through 2006 and dropped in 2007 (the GEM cancellation year). Three independent sources verified for 2005: Natural Gas Intel (trade press), BU Today/Boston University, and Friends of the Boston Harbor Islands.

Proposed year = when Energy Transfer first publicly announced the Blue Marlin deepwater crude-oil export port (offshore Cameron Parish, LA, tied to its Nederland, TX terminal). Energy Transfer announced the project in 2019; the formal MARAD/USCG deepwater-port application followed Oct 2020 (later milestone). One independent trade source (Tank Storage News America) verified for 2019 + Blue Marlin; the 2019 announcement is also reported by S&P Global Platts, RBN Energy and Hellenic Shipping News, but those pages bot-block the verifier (403/404), so a clean second independent corroboration could not be captured -- hence medium, not high.

Proposed year = when the Bluewater Texas deepwater crude-oil export port (offshore Corpus Christi/San Patricio County, TX) was first publicly proposed. Phillips 66 submitted the MARAD/USCG deepwater-port license application May 30, 2019; the Federal Register Notice of Application for 'Bluewater Texas Terminal LLC (Bluewater)' was published July 3, 2019. The Phillips 66/Trafigura JV under the Bluewater name was formalized Feb 2020 (later milestone). Single primary/regulatory source (Federal Register, 2019) verified for 2019 + Bluewater -- medium.

Terminal 2 is part of the same Bluewater Texas deepwater-port project as Terminal 1 (two SPM/VLCC berths under one application), so the same proposal year applies. Phillips 66 filed the MARAD/USCG deepwater-port license application May 30, 2019; Federal Register Notice of Application published July 3, 2019. Single primary/regulatory source (Federal Register, 2019) verified for 2019 + Bluewater -- medium.

Proposed year = when the crude/condensate oil terminal at the Port of Brownsville (now owned by JupiterMLP LLC) was first publicly launched. The project began as Centurion Terminals LLC, which leased acreage at the Port of Brownsville and broke ground on its oil-export/processing/storage terminal on Sept 10, 2015; Jupiter acquired Centurion's Brownsville assets in 2017. Two independent sources verified for 2015: Centurion's groundbreaking release (PR.com) and RGV Business Journal. Note: Sept 2015 was technically the groundbreaking, the earliest documented public year for the project.

BTH = Buckeye Texas Hub (Buckeye Texas Partners LLC, 80% Buckeye / 20% Trafigura), a crude/condensate/petroleum-products marine terminal on the Corpus Christi Inner Harbor (GEM mislabels it an 'LNG export terminal'; it is an oil/condensate terminal). Operating year = when the Buckeye Texas Partners complex commenced commercial operations: Buckeye's Dec 7, 2015 release states the integrated South Texas facility (condensate splitter plus deep-water marine terminal/LPG complex) was commissioned and generating revenue in 2015 (the marine-terminal complex was acquired from Trafigura in 2014). Single primary source (Buckeye Partners press release) verified for 2015 + Buckeye Texas. Caveat: GEM's BTH record is essentially blank, so the exact milestone is ambiguous; 2015 is the complex's commercial-operations start. Tier medium.

Could not pin a clean, citable year for when the Cameron LNG IMPORT/regasification terminal (Sempra, Hackberry, LA) was mothballed. The import terminal was built ~2005-2008 and opened for LNG imports ~2009, but US import demand collapsed and Sempra repurposed the site for LNG export (export FID 2014; export Trains began operating 2019-2020). No public source states a specific 'mothballed'/'imports ceased' year for the import unit -- regas capability was retained on paper while the facility pivoted to export, so the mothballing is not tied to a single sourced calendar year. Leaving UNRESOLVED rather than guess; needs manual determination of which year GEM's import-terminal 'mothballed' milestone refers to (candidates: ~2011 last import / 2014 export conversion).

Proposed year = when Commonwealth LNG (Cameron Parish, LA liquefaction/export facility) was first publicly proposed. Commonwealth entered the FERC pre-filing process in Aug 2017 (pre-filing docket PF17-9), its first major public proposal; the formal FERC Section 3 application followed Aug 2019 (docket CP19-502). Two independent sources verified for 2017 + Commonwealth: the Eversheds Sutherland LNG Law Blog (Aug 2017) and the DOE NEPA project page (DOE/EIS-0533, regulatory).

Operating year = when the Eagle Ford Terminals crude-oil marine terminal (Eagle Ford Terminals Corpus Christi LLC, a Plains All American / Enterprise Products JV) began operating. It received its first vessel at the new dock on Sept 10, 2019 (first-cargo/operations milestone). Verified across the Port of Corpus Christi (port-authority release) plus independent trade outlets Offshore Energy, BIC Magazine and Safety4Sea -- all PASS for 2019 + Eagle Ford. (This is an oil terminal, not LNG.)

Proposed year for the Eagle LNG Jacksonville (St. Johns River, FL) liquefaction/export terminal (T1-T3). Eagle LNG Partners Jacksonville LLC filed its DOE long-term LNG-export application (Docket 16-15-LNG) on Jan 27, 2016 -- the cleanest verifiable first formal public proposal of the export facility (FERC application Jan 2017; FERC authorization Sept 2019). Verified for 2016 + Eagle LNG via the Federal Register notice (2016-15694) and the DOE application PDF -- but these are two renderings of the SAME DOE filing (one origin), so independent:false / medium. Caveat: trade profiles state the project was 'in development since mid-2013', but those pages bot-block the verifier and that earlier date could not be independently confirmed; 2016 is the earliest robustly verifiable public-proposal milestone.
